title: Multiplexed enrichment and robust checkpointing for console telemetry stream
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Replace the existing single-pass console metrics ingest with a multiplexed enrichment layer that attaches route, tenant, and rollout metadata while providing robust, low-latency checkpointing to guarantee at-least-once processing with bounded duplicates. Scope: implement a shim between the ingest queue and downstream processors that performs parallel enrichments (user context lookup, rollout tags, model/route mapping) using a vectorized worker pool; persist per-shard offsets with a durable checkpoint store; surface per-shard lag + error metrics. Success metrics: 99.95% of events enriched and committed within 5s, deduplication rate <= 0.02% for end-to-end processed events, and less than 5% CPU increase on ingestion nodes for typical load profiles. Design notes: use a lightweight in-process RocksDB state store for prefix dedupe and short-lived joins; write checkpoints to DynamoDB with transactional writes to minimize coordinator complexity; implement a sharded watermark tracker so slow tenants do not stall other shards; enrichment calls should be non-blocking with a local LRU cache and a fallback circuit breaker to avoid cascading failures. The module must support canary routing (1% of traffic) and a quick kill switch to revert to the current pipeline. Metrics exported: per-shard processed_count, enrich_latency_p50/p95, checkpoint_commit_latency, shard_lag_seconds; traces for enrichment flow to Jaeger and logs to structured CloudWatch.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment layer deployed behind feature flag and serving 1% of ingestion traffic in canary
Durable per-shard checkpoints written to DynamoDB and used to resume processing after restarts
Per-shard lag and error metrics visible in Console (Prometheus -> Grafana dashboard) and alerting configured
E2E tests (k6) verifying enrichment correctness and dedupe rate under synthetic load
Rollback path documented and automated (kill switch + config toggle)
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff — scoped work with PM and Observability. Decided to prioritize low-latency enrichments and avoid a separate enrichment microservice to reduce hops. Action: prototype RocksDB-backed dedupe.

2026-03-04: Spike results — vectorized worker pool reduced p95 enrichment time by ~35% vs serial lookups; DynamoDB checkpoint writes add ~8ms median overhead per batch. Prototype PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/241

2026-03-06: Design review — Security flagged that tenant IDs and route metadata may contain PII in edge cases. Decision: redact fields via deterministic hashing before checkpointing; add automated schema sanitizer. Action: add security review requirement and contact security@redwood for sign-off.

2026-03-08: Integration test — ran k6 synthetic workload (100k events/min) against canary. Observed a tail-case where a downstream enrichment cache miss caused request fan-out and increased latency for that shard. Mitigation: implement per-shard concurrency limit + circuit breaker. Opened follow-up ticket ENG-42192 for cache telemetry improvements.

2026-03-11: PR feedback from runtime team — requested explicit backpressure contract (token-bucket) and clearer semantics for 'committed' vs 'acked' events. Response: updated design doc and added checkpoint commit state machine to the PR. PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/256

2026-03-12: Deployed canary to prod region eu-west-1 at 1% traffic. Early telemetry: enrich_latency_p95 = 420ms, checkpoint_commit_latency median = 12ms, no increase in error budget. Next: ramp to 5% after smoke window.
